idiom_name: try/finally or runExclusive around a typed async mutex
implementation_notes: TypeScript erases at runtime, so the platform analysis is JavaScript's: no lock primitive, run-to-completion for synchronous code, and explicit mutual exclusion only where a task suspends. What types add is a checkable contract: express the lock as a Mutex interface with runExclusive<T>(critical) (or acquire() returning a release function) so the release path is written once inside the implementation and callers cannot forget it. For cross-tab or cross-worker coordination, the Web Locks API and Atomics on SharedArrayBuffer remain the platform primitives, and worker_threads is where real parallelism lives.
pitfalls: Types cannot force a release: an interface with separate lock()/unlock() still lets callers omit the finally, so prefer runExclusive-shaped APIs.
Decorator-based @synchronized wrappers lock the whole method - including awaits, I/O and nested decorated calls, which deadlock when the same mutex is re-acquired.
async-mutex-style runExclusive is not reentrant, and a rejected critical function must still release (the library does; hand-rolled wrappers often do not).
Structural typing accepts any object with the right shape as a Mutex; verify the implementation, not just the type.
In worker_threads shared state requires SharedArrayBuffer plus Atomics (or transferring messages); typed objects over the structured clone algorithm are copies, so locking them is meaningless.
